questiontext.text:
Find the derivative of \(f(x) = {@fx@}\) at \(x = {@ee@}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.

\(f'({@ee@}) = \)[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
This question evaluates the use of all three basic differentiation rules combined. 

We will start by differentiating the function inside the logarithm for simplicity. In order to do so we will need to use the quotient rule and, when differentiating the numerator, we will have to use the product rule and the chain rule. We will do so directly, if you need further help please post a question in the issues forum.

If \(y = \displaystyle {@ins@}\) then 

\(y' = \displaystyle \frac{({@bot@})\cdot (1\cdot {@p2@} + x\cdot {@bb@}\cdot ({@x^2+aa@})^{@bb-1@}\cdot 2\cdot x) - {@top@}\cdot {@cc@} \cdot 3 \cdot x^2 }{({@bot@})^2}\)

\( = \displaystyle \frac{({@bot@})\cdot ({@p2@} + {@bb*x*2*x*(x^2+aa)^(bb-1)@}) - {@top*cc*3*x^2@}}{({@bot@})^2}\)

Here, we could keep trying to expand and simplify but since we want the value of the derivative at a point, there is no need to do so as we will simply substitute \(x={@ee@}\) into this expression later.

We now differentiate the whole function using the chain rule as follows:

\( \begin {align} \displaystyle f'(x) &= \displaystyle \frac{1}{{@ins@}} \cdot \displaystyle \frac{({@bot@})\cdot ({@p2@} + {@bb*x*2*x*(x^2+aa)^(bb-1)@}) - {@top*cc*3*x^2@}}{({@bot@})^2}\\ &=\displaystyle \frac{{@bot@}}{{@top@}} \cdot \displaystyle \frac{({@bot@})\cdot ({@p2@} + {@bb*x*2*x*(x^2+aa)^(bb-1)@}) - {@top*cc*3*x^2@}}{({@bot@})^2}\\ &=\displaystyle{@ratsimp(bot/top*(bot*(p2+bb*x*2*x*(x^2+aa)^(bb-1))-top*cc*3*x^2)/(bot^2))@}\\ &=\displaystyle{@ratsimp(dfx)@}\\ \end{align}\)

Once again, we could attempt to simplify but instead we will evaluate and then simplify to get 

\(f'({@ee@}) = {@ta@}\).
